rules.title: How it works
rules.1: Once a day. After the official {sym} close (Yahoo's final close, checked against Chainlink's price on Base within 1% and against Nasdaq's to the cent when Nasdaq has published it), the close is proposed on-chain, can be disputed for 6 hours, then settles. Requests made before the bell are filled at that close; later ones at the next. An entry can be taken back until 5 minutes before the bell (the 0.1 % entry fee is kept). In those last 5 minutes the site sends no entry, exit or cancel, so nothing you sign lands after the bell by surprise.
rules.2: Only the part someone bets against moves. The thinner side is fully matched, the crowded side pro rata. The unmatched part just holds the stock (moves 1:1 with it), so how much you move depends on the pool; it is always shown before you enter.
rules.3: Funding = 0.1 % a day × (long − short) ÷ (long + short), paid by the crowded side to the thin side, on the matched part only.
rules.4: No liquidations, no debt. One close beyond a tier's zero line takes that tier to zero, never below. Intraday prices never count.
rules.5: Everything compounds. Gains, losses and funding stay in your position. An entry is your position as soon as its close settles; an exit waits for you to withdraw it.
rules.6: Fees: 0.1 % in and 0.1 % out, taken in the token. They become the platform's hedge position.
rules.7: Issuer controls. The issuer of a stock token can pause it. Not available to persons in the United States.

h.title: Daily closes
h.intro: The pool settles once each trading day, on the official close. Every close goes on-chain with the sha256 of its price evidence, can be disputed for 6 hours while a second server re-checks it, and then settles. Press Check on any day to hash the evidence yourself.
